items.summary: Environment-Gaussian reflection path not ported: diff-surfel-tracing uses OptiX (optixModuleCreate), which has no ROCm equivalent. Core 3DGS rasterization path works.

EnvGS submodule AMD-Ecosystem/diff-surfel-tracing@moat-port is a clean GPU-validated OptiX->HIPRT port, but upstream xbillowy/diff-surfel-tracing re-licensed/rewrote history after EnvGS pinned gitlink 9b86cbf (now ahead 2, behind 3 = diverged). Decision needed: rebase port onto current upstream main vs PR against pinned base. Also LFS pointer-stub .dlls lack a .gitattributes.

Hold diff-surfel-rasterizations upstream PR until the standalone harness runs on gfx90a and gfx1201 (gfx1100 done: all 3 variants PASS -- finite img/grads, FD opacity slope 1.000, fit converges). Turnkey on each host: set PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=<gfx90a|gfx1201>, rebuild the 3 -wet variants (pip install -e), then python3 projects/EnvGS/validation/validate_diff_surfel_rocm.py ; expect PASS per variant (gfx90a ~95% loss drop / ~25-26dB). gfx1201 via Windows TheRock venv. Also still needs the pre-open squash to drop the 'Strategy-B' commit-message wording. Parent EnvGS already validated all 3 archs transitively.

Resolved 2026-08-06. Both submodules are in AMD-Ecosystem and both are cleared to contribute -- diff-surfel-tracing is MIT, and diff-surfel-rasterizations is cleared on the same basis as the other unlicensed projects. What still holds EnvGS is its own Inria-derived core, which is a question about EnvGS rather than about its submodules.

Rescan with the fixed scan_nvidia: EnvGS's own tree ships scripts/instant-ngp/colmap_to_nerf.py with the NVIDIA 'retain all intellectual property' proprietary notice (instant-ngp, NVIDIA Source Code License, non-commercial). Old-marker-matchable casing, so the original screen missed the path entirely. Needs a person's licence ruling; the vendored OptiX submodule headers are tracked with diff-surfel-tracing.
